title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. It is page 103 of the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), interleaved in the folder. The header 'IX' and page '103' both point to this.

First part, end of §9.2. The goal is the pairing (9.1.2). For abelian varieties A and A' (dual, or related by a biextension) over the fraction field of a henselian discrete valuation ring, (9.1.2) is an ℓ-adic pairing between the 'toric' parts of the monodromy data. Here M and M' are the character groups attached to the toric parts of the reductions, and Ǎ denotes duals. In the special case treated in 9.2, the biextension gives a canonical element u of (M̌'⊗M̌)⊗Z_ℓ. Two facts follow:
- u is invariant under inertia I.
- u is invariant under π_0 = π/I = Gal(k̄/k), because it is defined canonically and so is stable under transport of structure.

Through the identifications (M̌'⊗M̌⊗Z_ℓ)^I ≅ Hom_Z(M⊗M', Z_ℓ) ≅ Hom_{Z_ℓ}(M_ℓ⊗M'_ℓ, Z_ℓ), u is a bilinear form M_ℓ × M'_ℓ → Z_ℓ. This is the monodromy pairing (9.1.2). To define it in general, Grothendieck announces two preliminary sections.

Second part, §9.3 'Extensions panachées' (blended extensions). Let C be an abelian category and P, R, Q objects of C. Consider objects X with a three-step filtration X = X^0 ⊃ X^1 ⊃ X^2 ⊃ X^3 = 0 and given isomorphisms gr^0 ≅ P, gr^1 ≅ R, gr^2 ≅ Q. Such an X yields two ordinary extensions:
- F = X^1, an extension 0→P→F→R→0;
- E = X/X^2, an extension 0→R→E→Q→0.
The classification problem is: given E and F, describe the X inducing them. The continuation in SGA 7 shows that:
- such X exist iff the Yoneda product E∘F vanishes in Ext²(Q,P);
- the set of such X is a torsor (pseudo-torsor) under Ext¹(Q,P).
This is then used to define the monodromy pairing through the filtration T_ℓ ⊃ (fixed part) ⊃ (toric part) of Tate modules.
errors: The transcription drops an opening parenthesis in (9.2.9).
Minor grammatical slip in the original: 'munie' should agree with 'objets' ('munis').

ideas.what: Canonical I- and Gal(k̄/k)-invariant element u giving the ℓ-adic monodromy pairing between character groups of toric parts
Objects with a three-step filtration and identified graded pieces, classified relative to the two induced extensions
ideas.modern_name: Blended extensions (extensions panachées); obstruction is the Yoneda product in Ext², and the set of solutions is an Ext¹(Q,P)-torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 IX §9.3; later used by Deligne (Hodge III, 1-motives, mixed motives), Bertrand, Hain and others

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 IX, including the well-known §9.3 on extensions panachées. Nothing on it is unpublished. The only curiosity is archival: this page is filed inside the 1976 divided-power de Rham folder (cote 136).
transcription_corrections: (9.2.9) should read u ∈ ((M̌'⊗_Z M̌)⊗_Z Z_ℓ)^I, with an opening parenthesis missing in the transcription.
Hom_Z(M⊗M', Z_ℓ): the semicolon in the transcription should be a comma separating the arguments.
Line '421' is the archive stamp and '286' is the archive pencil numbering. Neither is part of the mathematics.
